title: SwiftUI layout system
summary: Layout in SwiftUI is a conversation: the parent proposes a size, the child picks its own size, then the parent places the child. Everything else follows from this rule.
body: **In simple words:** (1) Parent says "you can have up to this much space". (2) Child decides how big it actually wants to be. (3) Parent positions it. A child can ignore the offer - `Text` only takes what its words need.
**Flexible vs fixed views:** `Text` and non-resizable `Image` hug their content. `Color`, `Rectangle`, `Spacer` take all space offered. `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` makes something stretch.

**Stacks:** `HStack`, `VStack`, `ZStack` divide space among children; `layoutPriority` decides who gets space first. `LazyVStack`/`LazyHStack` create children only when visible (use for long scrolling content). `Grid` and `LazyVGrid` for grids.

**Reading sizes:** `GeometryReader` gives you the proposed size but takes all space - use sparingly. `onGeometryChange` is lighter. `ViewThatFits` picks the first layout that fits (e.g. HStack, else VStack).
**Custom layouts:** the `Layout` protocol (`sizeThatFits` + `placeSubviews`) - great for tag clouds/flow layouts without GeometryReader tricks.
**Accessibility:** layouts should adapt to large Dynamic Type sizes, e.g. switch HStack to VStack.
keyPoints: Parent proposes, child chooses, parent places.
Modifier order matters (`padding` then `background` vs the reverse).
Lazy stacks/grids for long content; normal stacks for small content.
Avoid GeometryReader in every row; use `Layout`, `ViewThatFits` or `onGeometryChange`.
Safe area: content respects it by default; `ignoresSafeArea()` for backgrounds.

code.caption: Adaptive layout without GeometryReader

mistakes: Wrapping views in GeometryReader just to get the screen width.
Using `VStack` inside `ScrollView` for thousands of items (creates all of them) instead of `LazyVStack`/`List`.
followups: **`List` vs `LazyVStack`?** List gives cell reuse, swipe actions, separators and system styling; LazyVStack gives full styling control.
**How would you build a tag/flow layout?** A custom `Layout` that wraps items to new rows.
